replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design states password login is the enrolment path; credential stuffing on that endpoint is concrete and distinct."},{"id":"T2","keep":false,"reason":"Same attack on plain-storage refresh token for account access as T4; token theft via filesystem/backup.","duplicateOf":"T4"},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Design says biometrics only unlock screen; local-only check bypass is a distinct attack on the biometric control."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Plain app storage of refresh token quoted; theft and replay against refresh endpoint is concrete."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Design shows single stored token with no rotation/revocation; persistent access after password change is a distinct harm."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Design keeps biometric result client-side; lack of device-bound evidence for disputes is specific to this design."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Distinct attack: OS-enrolled second biometric, no tooling or token theft; different actor and mechanism from T3."}]}
